_comment: HAND-AUTHORED FROM THE FIXTURE'S CONSTRUCTION. Never generated by running
either program, and never to be 'corrected' by pasting a program's output.
If EXPECTED is produced by a run, the suite cannot fail: two ports that
drift the same way both pass, and this project has already watched five
sum-preserving corruptions sail through 22 checks. The fixture has to be
able to say 'you are both wrong', and it can only do that if the numbers
came from somewhere other than the programs being tested.
So every figure below is followed by the arithmetic that produced it. A
reviewer can check this file against conformance/home/ with a pencil.
WHEN A PROGRAM DISAGREES WITH THIS FILE, THE PROGRAM IS WRONG UNTIL A
HUMAN RE-DERIVES THE ARITHMETIC AND SAYS OTHERWISE. Changing a number here
to make a suite go green is the one edit that destroys the whole point.

_how: Codex writes two usage figures per turn. `last_token_usage` is that
turn's delta; `total_token_usage` is a RUNNING TOTAL over the session
LINEAGE — not over the file. A resumed or forked session inherits its
parent's total, so a file's first record can already carry tokens that
were spent before that file existed.
Both readings are legitimate and must agree:
sum the deduped deltas   (deadreckon)
final total minus the inherited base, plus banked resets (starreckon)
input is counted NET OF CACHE: input_tokens - cached_input_tokens, floored
at 0. cache_read is min(cached, input). That is deadreckon's rule at
sessions.py:991-993 and it is the one both sides are held to.

codex-simple._tests: an ordinary session, plus ONE RE-EMITTED TURN (record 3 repeats record 2 byte for byte). Summing deltas must dedup it; assigning the final total is immune to it. Both land on the same number.

_arithmetic.cross_check: final total (250,50,30) minus base (0,0,0) = in 250-50=200, cr 50, out 30 — agrees

codex-fork._tests: A FORK. Its first record's total is (1020,505,102) while that record's own delta is only (20,5,2), so 1000/500/100 was inherited from the parent and was NOT spent in this file. This is the exact shape that over-counted 1,021,379,811 tokens across the real corpus — ten sibling forks sharing one 69,322,178 prefix counted it ten times.

codex-reset._tests: A MID-STREAM RESET: the running total restarts at record 4. This is the OPPOSITE-SIGNED failure to the fork — subtracting an inherited base and nothing else silently drops everything before the reset. Because the two errors have opposite signs, no single-direction assertion catches both, which is why both files are here.

_arithmetic.cross_check: segment one banks (100,20,10) at the reset; segment two contributes (10,0,1); (110,20,11) -> in 110-20=90, cr 20, out 11 — agrees

_identity_note: THE TWO PROGRAMS NAME A CODEX SESSION DIFFERENTLY, and the fixture records
it rather than hiding it. deadreckon derives the id from the rollout
FILENAME; starreckon takes payload.id out of session_meta. Totals are
unaffected here because each file carries one session, but a set
comparison of session ids across the two programs cannot succeed, and two
files sharing one payload.id would be counted as two sessions by one
program and one by the other.
This is a real difference, not a fixture artefact. It is listed so nobody

_how: A turn can appear more than once: resuming rewrites earlier turns into
the new file, and a subagent's turns are inlined into its parent. Both
copies carry the same message.id, so the reader dedups on it and credits
a RUNNING MAXIMUM per id rather than a first-or-last write.
One logical session, `claude-1`, is deliberately spread across two files
in one project, because the dedup has to hold across files and not only
within one.

claude-1._tests: m1 appears twice with SMALLER numbers the second time (the maximum must win, not the last write). m2 appears once in each file (the same turn rewritten by a resume — it must be counted once). m3 appears only in the second file (a genuinely new turn in a resumed session must still count).

_messages.m1: (10,5,2,3) in file 1, then (1,0,0,0) in file 1 — max keeps (10,5,2,3)
_messages.m2: (20,0,8,4) in file 1 AND in file 2 — one turn, counted once

_comment: THREE STATES, AND THEY ARE THE POINT. The single most repeated defect in
this system is two of these rendering as one number, seven times in four
disguises. A fixture that only checked arithmetic would miss every one of
them, because a store that was never read sums to zero just as neatly as
a store that is really empty.

claude.why: home/.claude/projects holds one project with two files

gemini.why: home/.gemini/tmp EXISTS and holds no session. Must NOT report as absent, and must NOT be indistinguishable from a store that was never looked at.

grok.why: there is deliberately no home/.grok. Must NOT report as a zero total — nothing was found because nothing is there.

bob.why: there is deliberately no home/.bob here. bob is SQLite, and on a Node older than 22.5 the builtin is missing — that case must report `unreadable`, NEVER 0, or an unsupported runtime looks exactly like an unused tool.

_how: A session whose TRANSCRIPT WAS DELETED and whose counters survived in
.claude.json. On the machine this was ported from, 4,172,332,033 tokens
across 78 sessions that nothing else in either program can see.
THE FIXTURE CARRIES ALL THREE TRAPS ON PURPOSE:
1. lastModelUsage RESTATES lastTotal* field for field. Every entry here
includes it. A reader that adds both reports exactly 2x.
2. orph-1 appears in THREE config files — the live one, an alt profile
with SMALLER numbers, and a backup with a duplicate. Summing per file
gives 240/24/2400/12; the maximum gives 100/10/1000/5. On the real
store the same mistake produced 759,975,256,912 against 4,172,332,033,
which is 182x.
3. claude-1's transcript is ALIVE (it is in the claude fixture above), so
it must be excluded or every live session is counted twice.
orph-zero has a lastSessionId and four zero counters — a project that was
opened and never spent anything. It is dropped, not emitted as a zero.

orph-1._arithmetic: per-field MAXIMUM across the three copies -> (100,10,1000,5); total 1115. Summing instead gives 2400+ and is the 182x bug in miniature.

_excluded.claude-1: its transcript is alive in the claude fixture — counting it here would double every live session
_excluded.orph-zero: all four counters are 0 — a counter that never ran is not a session

_how: Per-session rollups. The format has NO cache counters at all, so those
buckets are 0 because the data has no such field — not because the value
is zero. cs-empty records 0 and 0: a rollup with no tokens is not a
session and is not emitted. That distinction moves the session COUNT and
not the sum, so no sum-based check can see it — which is exactly how the
first port of this reader read 20 sessions against deadreckon's 18 while
both totalled 258,502,806.
Local models: counted, never billed. The counters live at the EXACT path
messages[].versions[].steps[].genInfo.stats.{promptTokensCount,
predictedTokensCount}. The first JS port searched the whole document for
any genInfo instead of walking that path — more permissive than
deadreckon, identical on every real file, and divergent on the first
malformed one. The fixture uses the real nesting so the exact path is
what gets exercised.
